data.body:
`make verify` at HEAD `3401b613dd201f23ca9ae36a9e2e9ef81744f810` returned RC=2 with a
single failure:

    tests/unit/test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py::test_the_trace_check_detects_maintenance_inside_a_commit
    rebar create failed (exit 1): Error: git commit failed while holding lock:
    git timed out after 30s

Root-caused as host contention, not a defect in this change. While that verify ran, this
session made concurrent tracker writes (`rebar edit --parent`, two `edit_ticket` writes,
and four link/unlink/`set_file_impact` MCP calls). Each auto-commits and pushes the
tickets branch, contending for the same repo-global git lock the test's real `rebar
create` needs. The test's commit lost that race and hit its 30s timeout.

Re-run in isolation with no concurrent tracker writes:
`tests/unit/test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py` -> **4 passed in 137.43s**, including
the test that failed.

This is not a `recheck`-style hand-wave: the whole module was re-run and the specific
assertion passed. The failure is not attributable to this change.

Related but NOT identical: closed bug `a16d-ad6f-d7ca-4f7f` records the same error family
(`git commit failed while holding lock`) as a concurrency race in the store under parallel
load. That one was a CI-load tree-build race; this one is a 30s lock timeout on a
developer host. Noted as adjacent prior art, not as the same defect.

Re-running the full `make verify` cleanly, with no tracker writes in flight, before push.

Operational note for this host: do not perform rebar tracker writes while `make verify`
runs anywhere in the repo. The guidance already forbids running a gate op from a worktree
under verify; these tracker writes are repo-global and contend the same way.
